sentences.text: Astronauts float in orbit. Must mean gravity has left the chat, right? Not even close.
At space station heights, Earth's gravity is still about ninety percent as strong as at the surface. So what's holding everyone up?
Nothing. The station, its crew, and the objects inside are all in free fall together. They appear to float relative to each other.
But the station is also moving sideways so fast that its falling path curves around Earth. It keeps missing the ground.
Imagine throwing a ball faster and faster, high above the atmosphere. With the right sideways speed, continuous falling becomes an orbit.
An astronaut's mass hasn't disappeared. But in ideal free fall, a scale would read zero. Weightless doesn't mean gravity-free.
So, is an astronaut floating... or falling with a truly outstanding record of missing the floor?
